answer: Agents earn a vested reputation stake paid out in small slices over many epochs; identity weight and rewards unlock gradually, so a flood of cheap new accounts can only touch the outer ripple of the reward pool while their stake stays locked. A sybil attacker fronting copper for thousands of forged identities finds the spiral working against them: any account caught or abandoned before vesting completes forfeits most accrued earnings, so flash-farming collapses because exit costs exceed injected capital.
